note: KEGG-derived tables are never committed to any repo (KEGG data are for academic use only). The .tsv and info.txt files here are therefore SYNTHETIC stand-ins, not KEGG data: they reuse the row format of the recorded KEGG REST bodies (tab-separated 'namespace:id<TAB>namespace:id' for conv/link, 'id<TAB>name' for list, the 'name count YYYY/MM/DD' lines of info/kegg) with every KEGG entry and pathway id renamed into an unused range by an order-preserving bijection (C0nnnn/C1nnnn -> C9nnnn, D0nnnn -> D9nnnn, map0nnnn -> map9nnnn, map07nnn -> map07(nnn+700), hsa0nnnn -> hsa9nnnn) and every pathway name replaced by a placeholder. PubChem SIDs/CIDs, InChIKeys, ChEBI ids and NCBI gene ids (hsa:<entrez>) are real public identifiers. Never add real KEGG rows here; tests that need real tables read the staged reference folder on the cluster (opt-in).

format_source.info.txt: format of GET https://rest.kegg.jp/info/kegg (synthetic counts; release dates kept so the release-string test is realistic)
format_source.list_pathway_hsa.tsv: format of GET https://rest.kegg.jp/list/pathway/hsa (names keep the ' - Homo sapiens (human)' suffix)

recorded_responses.pubchem_sid_cids_standardized.json: POST https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/substance/sid/cids/JSON?cids_type=standardized with sid=<the 11 SIDs in the conv tables> (complete response; SID 7847124 has no standardized CID)
